issues.legal_issue: A person who loses legal control of vacant land through delivery of possession in execution may seek adjudication of their claim under the execution procedure even if they were not physically present on the land when possession was delivered.
material_facts: The objectors claimed to have purchased the vacant land under registered sale deeds, obtained possession as recorded in those deeds, and had their names entered in municipal records.
The decree holder obtained delivery of the land through the court in execution of a decree for specific performance.
The objectors were not physically present on the land when possession was delivered, but the delivery deprived them of their claimed control over it.

The executing court heard evidence and decided the objectors’ application, while the High Court held that the application was not maintainable because there had been no actual and physical dispossession.
issues.conclusion: The objectors’ loss of control over the vacant land through delivery to the decree holder amounted to dispossession for purposes of their application. Their application was maintainable, and the executing court could adjudicate the competing claims to the property rather than require a separate suit.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rules 99 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure provide for an application following dispossession and require relevant questions, including questions of right, title, or interest, to be determined by the executing court rather than by a separate suit; Rule 103 treats the resulting order as a decree for appeal. The amended execution procedure was intended to reduce multiplicity and delay. Possession is context-dependent: for vacant land, control and the power to exclude others may establish possession even without physical presence. The Court relied on Shreenath v. Rajesh, Brahmdeo Chaudhary v. Rishikesh Prasad Jaiswal, Silverline Forum Pvt. Ltd. v. Rajiv Trust, Tanzeem-E-Sufia v. Bibi Haliman, and Bhag Mal v. Ch. Parbhu Ram.

rule.if: execution_third_party_claim and vacant_land and claimed_control_supported_by_possession_evidence and court_delivery_transferred_control

predicates.execution_third_party_claim: A person other than the judgment debtor sought adjudication of a claim to property in an execution proceeding.
predicates.vacant_land: The property at issue was vacant land whose possession could be exercised through control over it.
predicates.claimed_control_supported_by_possession_: The applicant relied on evidence such as transaction documents recording delivery of possession and entries in public records to support a claim of control over the land.
predicates.court_delivery_transferred_control: The court delivered possession to the decree holder in a way that deprived the applicant of the applicant’s claimed control over the land.

issues.definition: When a third-party claim in execution concerns vacant land, is supported by evidence of control, and court delivery transfers that control, the claim may be heard by the executing court despite the applicant’s physical absence.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court that reverses an executing court’s decision solely on a threshold objection, without deciding contested issues on the merits, must have those merits issues determined on remand.
material_facts: The executing court rejected the preliminary objection to maintainability and decided the contested issues concerning the parties’ knowledge of the competing transactions.
The High Court allowed the decree holder’s appeal on the ground that the objectors had not been physically dispossessed and did not address the merits in detail.
The Supreme Court held that the High Court had not determined the merits issues that required reconsideration as the first appellate court on facts and law.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and remanded the case to it to decide the appeal afresh, including the unresolved merits issues.
issues.legal_principle: The Supreme Court stated that the merits issues were liable to be re-examined by the appellate court as the first court of facts and law. Because the High Court had disposed of the appeal on maintainability without addressing those issues, the case had to be remanded for decision in accordance with law.

predicates.execution_order_appeal: An appeal concerned an order made in an execution proceeding.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_on_threshold_gr: The appellate court reversed the executing court’s order solely on a threshold objection.
predicates.merits_issues_left_undecided: The appellate court did not determine contested issues on the merits that required its consideration.

issues.definition: When an appellate court reverses an execution order on a threshold ground and leaves material merits issues undecided, the appeal is remanded for those issues to be determined.
